content.title: About
content.content: Mixed nuts, honey roasted, is a blend of almonds, hazelnuts, cashews, walnuts and peanuts coated with a thin layer of honey glaze and lightly roasted to a golden hue. The nuts retain their characteristic flavors while the honey adds sweetness and aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The honey glaze helps keep the nuts crunchy longer by slowing fat oxidation.
Mixed nut blends are popular in backpacking meals because of their high energy density.
Honey can be substituted with maple syrup for a vegan version.
Some mixes include dried fruit or spices, but this product uses only pure honey.

items.title: Rich in healthy fats
items.content: Nuts provide monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids that support heart health.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: The nuts contain thiamine, riboflavin and niacin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Honey and nuts are high in flavonoids and polyphenols that combat free radicals.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: The combination of protein, fiber and fat helps maintain a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Provides minerals
items.content: Nuts supply magnesium, phosphorus, zinc and iron, essential for many bodily functions.

items.title: Tree nut allergy
items.content: The product contains several types of nuts, which can trigger severe allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: High in calories
items.content: Honey‑roasted nut mixes are calorie‑dense, so moderation is recommended.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Honey adds natural sugars, which may be a concern for people with diabetes or low‑sugar diets.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: Small nuts can pose a choking risk for young children.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the honey‑roasted mixed nuts as a snack, stir them into granola, yogurt, baked goods, or sprinkle over salads for a crunchy boost.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct light. For extended storage, refrigerate to prevent the fats from becoming rancid.
